messages: /tokenwise:route implement a feature from a written spec, about 12 files
/tokenwise:route review a six-file diff in a repo I know well

result:
- **Phase:** Implement from a written spec, about 12 files.
- **Model and effort:** `/model sonnet` then `/effort medium`. On the bench, Sonnet at medium passed every run at 17% of the cost of Opus at xhigh, which also passed every run. That bench was a small test project, so 12 files is more than it tested.
- **Boundary:** Make sure the spec is saved to a file, then `/clear`, then switch. Switching after `/clear` costs nothing. If you switch without clearing, your whole current context gets re-processed on the new model; `/context` shows how big that is. This answer stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so it costs least if you clear right after reading it.
- **Delegate:** Hand the reading of existing code around those 12 files, test runs and log reading to subagents so only summaries come back. To run them on Haiku, set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` (Claude Code 2.1.257 or later) before starting the session. Keep the actual code writing in the main session.
- **Done when:** The full test suite is green, including the tests the spec asks for, and `git diff --stat` shows no edits to test files that already existed.
- **You give up:** Sonnet at medium makes fewer tool calls and thinks less than Opus. Across 12 files it's more likely to miss how the files interact, or an edge case the spec only implies.
- **Escalate when:**
  - **It didn't try hard enough** (skipped files, didn't run tests, stopped partway): stay on Sonnet and raise effort with `/effort high`, then `xhigh`.
  - **It had the context and still got it wrong** (misread the spec, wrong design): switch to `/model opus` at `/effort medium`, then `xhigh`. Switch at a `/clear` so the cache isn't re-processed.
  - **The spec turns out to be ambiguous:** stop and treat it as planning, with `/model opus` at `/effort high`.

- **Phase:** review a six-file diff in a repo you know well.
- **Model and effort:** `/model opus` then `/effort low`. The evidence for this comes from `claude-opus-5`, which is what `opus` pointed to on 8 September 2026. The test diff was also six files.
- **Boundary:** run `/clear` first, then switch. If you switch from another model with the session still going, your whole current context gets re-processed, and `/context` shows how big that is. After `/clear` the switch costs nothing. This answer stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so routing just before one is cheapest.
- **Delegate:** six files is small enough that you don't need to. If you want the tests run against the change, give that to a subagent so only the pass/fail summary comes back.
- **Done when:** all six files have been read, and every finding has a file:line plus the input or state that triggers it.
- **You give up:** low effort makes fewer tool calls, so it's less likely to check callers, config or tests outside the diff. In the test run that didn't cost anything. Opus at low found all five planted bugs in 3 turns, and opus at high found the same five in 13 turns for 3.3x the cost. Going down to Sonnet saves more but catches less: Sonnet at high missed one of the five bugs in two runs out of three.
- **Escalate when:**
  - It skips one of the six files, or gives findings without a file:line. Stay on opus and run `/effort high`.
  - The diff reaches into parts of the repo you don't know well. Same fix, `/effort high`.
  - It read the relevant code and still missed a bug you can point to. That's when you change the model. There's no test data for a model above opus on reviews.
